variants.title: 吹き抜けの蒸留工房
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: final rank-5 scene concept for an iPhone lofi focus app; one complete tall portrait illustration, approximately 9:19.5 aspect ratio, edge to edge.
Input image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not a scene to edit. Make an entirely new scene about a fully grown magical potion workshop.
STYLE MUST MATCH THE REFERENCE: intricate atmospheric pixel-art illustration, visible pixel clusters and stepped edges, restrained pixel texture, deep blue-violet shadows, warm amber practical lamps, small luminous cyan/green liquid accents, layered spatial depth. The small woman must be rendered with exactly the same pixel-art treatment and scale logic as the environment; do not paste a smooth anime character into pixel scenery. Not watercolor, not photorealistic, not a 3D miniature, not vector art, not flat primitive 8-bit art.
This is GROWTH TYPE: the finished elaborate workshop grew from a shabby table with one flask; use convincing connected equipment, added shelves, pipes, tiers and construction, not a landscape hidden by fog. Show the complete rank-5 workshop in this image, with no unrevealed black mask. Rich but coherent design, clear large silhouettes before small details; restful lofi atmosphere, no danger or explosive magic.
One young adult woman quietly doing her potion-making job at a modest workbench near the bottom; she is a small supporting figure, at most 13–15 percent of the full image height, with a very small head, black or dark brown hair tied back, practical apron. Her hands have a simple believable working pose with a notebook and small flask. The environment is the main subject.
Allow a small calm darker area toward the upper left for future UI, but DO NOT draw any UI, text, labels, status bar, time, icons, phone frame, border, collage panels, titles or watermarks. No other people. No oversized person, close-up portrait, giant cauldron character, or silver bob hairstyle.

SCENE A: An interior looking into a tall, cozy, timber-and-brick distillery with a three-storey open atrium. The composition climbs vertically from the small original oak workbench below to an elaborate copper-and-glass potion apparatus above. An impressive central translucent pear-shaped glass vessel contains softly glowing turquoise liquid; branched glass condensers, rounded tanks, copper coils, gravity-fed funnels and tidy bottle-filling racks connect logically around it. Upper wooden galleries, narrow stairs and shelves full of differently shaped small bottles make the workshop feel fully grown and productive. Amber hanging lamps illuminate wood and copper, indigo recesses remain quiet. The woman works at a little bench in the lower left, not at the center. Make the central machinery and layered interior the visual attraction. Cinematic but intimate, no exterior city view.

SCENE B: A fantastical apothecary workshop built inside the enormous hollow of an old tree, viewed through a generous open cutaway into the space, not a diagram. Broad curved timber walls and living roots form an intimate tall room with several irregular mezzanines. An elaborate distillation system winds upward with the tree: glass bulbs suspended between branches, copper pipes following the wood, herb-drying racks, rounded bottle cabinets, a small upper greenhouse with medicinal leaves, and a large luminous mint-green infusion chamber nested in the trunk. Moss, climbing medicinal plants and warm small lanterns weave around the equipment. Tiny controlled mauve liquid accents contrast with amber light and deep indigo shadows, matching the reference pixel rendering. The small dark-haired woman works at the original simple desk tucked into the lower right root alcove. This is a mature, highly equipped potion-making workplace; machinery, branches and shelves should interlock organically. Avoid a generic fairy cottage or a view dominated by a forest.

SCENE C: Exterior and open-front view of a fully developed potion-making mill beside a narrow canal at blue hour. A compact but intricate tall cluster of attached timber-and-stone workshop rooms rises above the water, with warm illuminated windows, exterior wooden galleries, a large slow waterwheel, and beautifully connected copper pipes and glass apparatus crossing between floors. A rooftop greenhouse holds medicinal plants. Translucent cylindrical tanks, a small line of bottle-filling nozzles, coiled glass condensers and glowing cyan liquid channels reveal that the buildings together form one complex potion workshop. Look from an intimate slightly elevated oblique view along the canal, so foreground water and steps lead into the tall building. Warm amber rooms reflect in dark violet water. This must feel peaceful and handmade, neither a city skyline nor a futuristic chemical plant.
